First, I need to break down each component. Request routing involves how requests are directed to different parts of the cluster. Maybe using a queuing system like a priority queue or a round-robin. Queueing would be about how data is stored and processed. Tail latency is the time a request spends waiting for the tail to process, which could be affected by the queue length and processing speed.

Cache transfer is about how data moves between the cache and main memory. Latency here would be the time taken for data to move, which could be minimized by efficient cache management. Role switching refers to when the system switches between different roles (like decoding or processing) to handle different tasks. Batch completion would be the time taken for multiple requests to complete, which depends on the number of tasks and their processing speed.

GPU utilization is about how much GPU resources are being used, which affects throughput. Throughput tradeoffs involve balancing between processing power and efficiency, maybe through optimization techniques.
